The timing of the stages and the shape of the settlement curve are illustrative (rapid at first, then slowing settlement after each stage).

The northern bypass of Kaposvár crosses a fishpond over a 150 m long section. Here there is 5.5–7 m of loose, water-saturated organic sediment (peat, organic silt) with a water content of 260–500%. Soil replacement would have been too expensive, so the 5–12 m high embankment was built in stages with counterweight berms: the next stage could only be placed once consolidation under the previous one had progressed sufficiently. On average 20–25% of the fill material only made up for the settlement – under a 12 m high embankment this means 2.4–3 m of compression.
